rubrics.criterion: No remaining class or state-bearing owner object in the file-tree layer concentrates the whole workspace lifecycle: the directory scan/metadata handling, tree sort ordering, in-memory pruning, and create/rename/delete lifecycle are not all owned by one body after the patch.
rubrics.rationale: This case's concentrated owner (src/utils/workspace.ts WorkspaceService, imported by six production files) is the exact relation the task asks to dissolve; a patch that leaves an equivalent omnibus owner (renamed, re-typed, or re-housed in a module object) has not resolved the instance's central problem.

rubrics.criterion: The responsibilities are placed in at least three distinct, focused homes (e.g., dedicated modules or small owner units), such that no single home owns both the recursive directory walk and the file create/rename/delete mutations (order handling and pruning belong to units other than whichever unit walks directories).
rubrics.rationale: The task prompt names scan/metadata, ordering, pruning, and lifecycle as the distinct concerns of this instance; the boundaries exist in the injected code because the absorbed pieces came from different modules (getFileMeta, Root's comparator, File/Tree/App handlers), so a genuine split must re-establish at least those separations.

rubrics.criterion: The sort-comparator unit receives its sort options at call time (from its caller or parameters) rather than reading mutable ordering state stored on a long-lived shared owner instance that other operations also mutate through.
rubrics.rationale: In the injected state compare/sortFn/sortTree read a shared activeSort field set by sortTree calls from the Root component; decoupling ordering from that cross-operation state is the cleanest resolution of this instance's coupling, though a repair can still be correct with different parameter plumbing.

rubrics.criterion: All former call sites of the dissolved service were rewired to the new focused homes: the zustand fetchDir action, the project workspace screen's scan and add-file handling, the Root component's sort effect, the File component's rename and delete handlers, and the Tree component's delete handler no longer call the central workspace owner.
rubrics.rationale: In this instance the injected owner is consumed at exactly those six places (src/store/appStore.ts, src/components/Project/App.tsx, src/components/Project/FileTree/Root.tsx, File.tsx, Tree.tsx, plus the two utility shims); unwiring every one of them is required for the separation to be real rather than nominal.

rubrics.criterion: The existing utility module contracts keep functioning after the patch: the exported getFileMeta entry-metadata function and the default-exported removePath tree-pruning function still resolve for their existing importers (as real implementations or equivalent semantic homes), and the FileInfo type remains importable from a production module.
rubrics.rationale: These two module APIs predate the injected owner in this repository and are imported by the file-tree components and the store; the task's compatibility boundary explicitly requires them to keep working, so silently dropping the exports without rewiring importers breaks the build contract.

rubrics.criterion: The recursive scan walk is no longer duplicated: the store's fetchDir and the project workspace screen's file loading consume one shared scanning implementation instead of each carrying an inline copy of the directory walk.
rubrics.rationale: The clean-state codebase duplicated the identical processEntries walk in fetchDir and the project screen's getFiles - the consolidation opportunity this instance's repair legitimately seizes while it is already touching both call sites.

rubrics.criterion: src/utils/workspace.ts is removed once its functionality has been relocated, including its service exports and its re-exported type surface, and no other production module still imports from it.
rubrics.rationale: The injected owner module is the artifact this task exists to eliminate; leaving a dead or near-empty service module behind (or orphan imports of it) is incomplete cleanup for this instance even when behavior is preserved.

rubrics.criterion: No utility function keeps a pass-through body whose entire implementation only delegates to another unit while keeping the old name for import compatibility (a getFileMeta/removePath-shaped forwarding shim) - restored callables must contain their real implementation logic again, or their importers must be rewired and the shim deleted.
rubrics.rationale: The injected state is recognizable exactly by getFileMeta and removePath having been hollowed into one-line delegations to the central owner; the task prompt explicitly forbids leaving such pass-through forwarding behind, while still permitting the names to live on as real implementations.

rubrics.criterion: Former call sites drop Tauri interop imports they no longer use (readDir, exists, createDir, removeDir, removeFile, renameFile, writeTextFile, join and similar) so no file-tree component or store imports filesystem primitives directly once that work lives in the focused units.
rubrics.rationale: In this instance the injection deliberately deleted those primitive imports from the components and store because the owner had absorbed them; a repair that re-extracts focused homes and then leaves stray unused primitive imports at the call sites leaves recognizable residue of the old arrangement.

rubrics.criterion: Directory scanning behavior is preserved: dot-prefixed entries are skipped, only .md files are kept among plain files, directories are still walked recursively, kept entries still carry metadata, and fetchDir still does nothing when no project is selected.
rubrics.rationale: These filtering and metadata semantics are the observable output of this instance's scan path (the walk now sealed inside the owner); they are easy to drop during extraction and are asserted by the repository's behavior expectations.

rubrics.criterion: Tree ordering results are unchanged: sorted output matches for Name, CreatedAt, and UpdatedAt in both ascending and descending directions, sorting still happens in place including nested children, and the date comparisons still invert between ascending and descending as the shared compare helper did.
rubrics.rationale: The injected owner swallowed the file tree's comparator and the visible sort popover drives it; a wrong extraction (e.g., inverting the direction or dropping the nested-child recursion) would silently reorder the user-visible file tree in both this repository's semantics and its tests

rubrics.criterion: The file lifecycle keeps its details: creation still suffixes .md, materializes the missing parent folder (via join(newfilePath, "../")) and writes an empty markdown file; rename still suffixes .md and renames within the entry's parent directory; deletion still removes directories recursively but files singly; and the deleted entry is still pruned from the in-memory tree returned to the store.
rubrics.rationale: These quirks are the concrete behavior of the create/rename/delete handlers this instance relocates and are exactly where a plausible-looking rewrite would simplify away real behavior.

rubrics.criterion: Open-file bookkeeping around rename is preserved: after renaming, the tree is refetched and the currently open file entry is updated to the new path and suffix-corrected name (with empty children) when the renamed file was the selected one, matching the pre-existing behavior in File.tsx.
rubrics.rationale: In this instance the injected renameEntry returns {path, name} precisely so File.tsx can update the open editor file; a repair that restructures the rename flow can silently drop the selected-file update, leaving a stale editor target.

rubrics.criterion: The patch does not alter the sort-settings flow it was not asked to change: sortInfo persistence via the settings store (setSortInfo calls and their persistence pockets), the sort popover's rendering and wiring, and the store's setSortInfo/fetchDir action signatures stay as they were outside the rewired internals.
rubrics.rationale: Sort persistence in this repository has its own design (persisted via @/utils/appStore setSortInfo) that the injected owner deliberately did not absorb; a repair that rewires extra state or changes the store's public action surface would be unrequested scope creep with regression risk.
